beats: Hook (p9): two circuits compute exactly the same 16-by-16 matrix with the same seven gates; on a real chip one needs three SWAPs and the other needs one; a compiler that decides the circuit before it looks at the chip will often pick wrong (line_qc_recipe_twin_cards: two different recipes, the same cake). Cast as in QC03-01: the planner = the compiler, the four hatted guests = the four qubits; new prop: one coin = the parity being gathered, the dial = the rotation R.

Her analogy (p9, clip 14:22-15:22): y = x*2 + 3 + t computed by two different three-address codes, the same answer in different steps (code letters the two columns on paper; reuse line_qc_recipe_twin_cards).

The insight (16:46-18:07): the CNOTs gather the parity of the qubits onto one qubit, R rotates by that parity, the mirror CNOTs undo the gathering. The coin is a light stand-in: each handoff is one CNOT, and the dial is turned one way or the other by what the coin shows (line_qc_recipe_coin_chain). Honest caveat in the voice: nothing is copied or looked at; the parity is held by a qubit, not read out. Parity gates are done properly in QC05-06.

Chain vs tree (p9, 18:39-19:34): the same seven gates, depth 7 vs 5: the chain hands the coin on one step at a time, the tree does two handoffs at once (line_qc_recipe_coin_chain vs line_qc_recipe_coin_tree). In general (Q25-04 p5, 08:12-10:12; tape it): N gates and depth N vs 2N-1 gates and depth 2logN+1.

On a real coupling graph (p10-p11, 20:33-25:58; tape p11): for the same starting placement one recipe needs 3 SWAPs, the other 1: pick the tree that fits where the qubits already sit (line_qc_recipe_swap_scramble: left half, three swaps of chaos; right half, one calm swap; reuse line_qc_pass_seat_swap). Clip 25:32-25:58: both are equivalent, choose the one the mapping favours.

Modular passes vs co-design (clip 23:09-23:34): a compiler that picks the recipe before it looks at the chip (line_qc_recipe_blinkers) vs one that picks it with the chip in view (line_qc_recipe_both_plans).

Paulihedral (Li, ..., Ding, ASPLOS 2022; tape p12, 28:55-30:04): fewer gates and lower depth than TKET on chemistry and physics simulation programs, on superconducting and ion-trap-like layouts; numbers only from the paper via FACTS.md. Honest limit: it takes longer to compile (line_qc_recipe_long_night). Soften the "adopted by IBM Qiskit" line (p13) unless the integration path is verified.
Takeaway (30:36-30:56): keep the high-level structure through the compiler instead of flattening it into gates early (line_qc_recipe_puzzle_sections).

Cover (line_qc_cover_03_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the four guests twice, once in a line passing one coin, once as two pairs passing coins at once; the planner between them holds up two recipe cards.
